what: Public AI-lab and AI-assisted mathematics claims from June to November 2026, each with its formal artefact, its outside checks, cert-machine's verdict where one exists and a pointer to the record that holds it. Read on 2026-11-04: the outside facts from the public sources each row cites (confidence C confirmed at the primary source, P partly, U unconfirmed); cert-machine's verdicts from the records each row points to, re-resolved at every build.

patterns.title: The statement is not the headline
patterns.line: The checked statement is a different object, a weaker or partial statement, has a moved clause, an old or degenerate target, or is missing, so the proof can pass while the headline stays unchecked.

patterns.title: Custom definitions are trusted
patterns.line: Machine models, encodings and definitions written in the challenge file, and Comparator definition holes compared by type only, are part of what a reader must trust.

patterns.title: One kernel, one party
patterns.line: The second kernel is mostly off, checks are run by the claimant or graded by AI, and the few rebuilds often vendor the claimant's construction modules.

patterns.title: Floats and tolerances in the checker
patterns.line: Numerical certificates were checked with floating-point verifiers, tolerances, sampling grids or one-sided validators.

patterns.title: Existence without a witness
patterns.line: Objects are proved to exist and never shown, or a disproof is non-effective.

patterns.title: Large computations nobody has replayed
patterns.line: The cost of replaying a search or a build (pod-hours, memory, unreleased tooling) is itself the open gap.

patterns.title: Missing files and checkers that stop short
patterns.line: Matrices, certificate files, witnesses, execution archives and ancillary files are not published, or a shipped checker skips what it names.

patterns.title: Gaps the claimant declares
patterns.line: Some claimants list their own gaps by design, and those declared gaps become the audit's reading list.

patterns.title: Credit and novelty, not correctness
patterns.line: Literature rediscovery, priority disputes and withdrawals bear on credit rather than on whether a checked statement holds.

steps.text: Both labs' Lean proofs check against their own statements, on two kernels each.
OpenAI's theorem implies Anthropic's ETHIsFalse, kernel-checked inside OpenAI's Lean 4.34.1 (Hawkley's chain, nanoda on); the seam to Anthropic's Lean 4.33.1 is read, not decided.

complexitylib's native ¬ETH on cslib's deterministic multitape Turing machine with the binary encoding encCNF (PR #1338) decided here: built from source, the three standard axioms from our own file, nanoda accepting all 49,025 declarations beneath not_eth, leanchecker --fresh exit 0. It formalizes OpenAI's Proposition 6.4 route as a native re-proof, not a bridge from either lab's own statement.

¬ETH on the word RAM at logarithmic word size (claimbox lean/eth-bridge, proof by an AI agent) decided here: the statement byte-equal to our pin, the three standard axioms, nanoda accepting all 49,735 declarations beneath not_eth_ram, leanchecker --fresh, and three planted wrong variants refused. complexitylib's own TM-to-RAM inclusions need polynomial time; the space-based address bound is the new step.

Anthropic's ETHIsFalse implies complexitylib's ¬ETH on cslib's multitape TM with encCNF, so both labs' own statements reach the standard machine (with Hawkley's chain). Proved in claimbox lean/eth-bridge by an AI agent; being decided here.

That any formal ETH (ours, cslib's, a lab's) is the textbook ETH is a reading of a definition. It stays one; the best outcome makes it a reading of a standard multitape machine and a word RAM with a reasonable binary encoding.
